reclamation.why: §546(c) (library bc_503b9_546c.md): a seller may reclaim goods received by the debtor while insolvent within 45 days before the petition by written demand not later than 45 days after receipt, or within 20 days after the petition if the 45 days expire after commencement. Insolvency in the prepetition window is presumed (§547(f)). Goods window: 2026-01-24 through 2026-03-10. QUALIFYING GOODS ONLY — the library states services, freight and handling are not 'goods': MS-7740 steel coil received 02-04 (62,400 invoiced, 36,800 paid 02-27, 25,600 unpaid), MS-7788 structural steel received 02-20 (41,300 unpaid), MS-7815 steel coil received 03-04 (36,800 unpaid); unpaid reclaimable-goods value 25,600+41,300+36,800 = 103,700. MS-7802 (freight & handling, 6,900) and MS-7819 (on-site cutting services, 14,400) do not qualify; MS-7701 (received 01-14) is outside the window and paid. DEADLINE: for all three in-window deliveries the 45-days-after-receipt date (03-21, 04-06, 04-18) falls after the 03-10 commencement, so the library's 20-days-after-petition rule controls — a conforming WRITTEN demand is due 2026-03-30. Mesa's 03-12 'FINAL NOTICE' is not a reclamation demand (it demanded money, not return of goods) and the 03-18 email only threatened to hold shipments. CAVEATS: the library states reclamation here is subject to the DIP lender's blanket lien, and the client cannot confirm the steel remains at Redwood (03-19: no additional information) — if it was cut or consumed there is nothing left to reclaim; a specific goods-identifiability condition is reclamation doctrine outside the library (UNVERIFIED, flagged not cited — conservative to confirm anyway). Practical recovery may be near zero. A conforming demand costs a letter and preserves the right: decide by 03-27, serve by 03-30.

ordinary_course_defense.reasoning: 90-day window is 2025-12-10 through 2026-03-10; four transfers total 180,000: 51,000 on 12-18 (ACH, 45 days after MS-7612), 44,000 on 01-22 (ACH, 43 days, MS-7655), 48,200 on 02-10 (ACH, 29 days, MS-7701), 36,800 on 02-27 (WIRE, 25 days, MS-7740 — the payment ledger itself notes 'WIRE — demanded by Mesa credit mgr'). 12-month history Apr–Nov 2025: six ACH payments of 38,700–45,200, all 43–47 days after invoice on NET-45 terms. Library: payments made under shortened terms, pressure, or unusual methods (wire on demand) compared with the parties' history generally fall outside §547(c)(2)(A). PROTECTED 95,000 = 12-18 (51,000: timing, method and sequence match the history exactly) + 01-22 (44,000: 43 days and ACH match history despite the 01-20 NET-15 email — kept protected on the history match, but flagged as the debtor's next-best target). EXPOSED 85,000 = 02-10 (paid in 29 days vs a 43–47 day history, two days after Lori's 01-20 'NET 15 / oldest invoice first or no shipments' ultimatum — shortened terms plus pressure) + 02-27 (a wire on demand — the library's own example of an unusual method, made to unlock shipments). Mesa bears the burden on all §547(c) defenses (§547(g)). §547(c)(2)(B) (ordinary industry terms) is undeveloped — no industry data in the library.

preference.new_value_notes: §547(c)(4): new value given after the transfer, unsecured, and on account of which the debtor did not make an otherwise unavoidable transfer. Wholly-unpaid deliveries after the two exposed transfers: MS-7788 41,300 (02-20) + MS-7802 6,900 (02-26) + MS-7815 36,800 (03-04) + MS-7819 14,400 (03-09) = 99,400 ≥ 85,000 exposed (services count as new value; the §503(b)(9) goods-only rule does not apply here). Backward application verified arithmetically: the 02-27 wire (36,800) is covered by 36,800+14,400 = 51,200 delivered after it; the 02-10 payment (48,200) is covered by 41,300+6,900 = 48,200 delivered after it. Every exposed dollar is covered, so new_value_defense = 85,000 and net_exposure_estimate = 0; worst case if (c)(4) fails outright = 85,000. Even at full avoidance of all 180,000, Jan–Mar deliveries total 210,000 and MS-7701 (48,200) plus the paid portion of MS-7740 survive as new value because they were paid only by the avoidable transfers — avoidable payments do not extinguish new value; backward application covers all four transfers. Residual risks: §547(g) burden; §502(d) disallows Mesa's entire 125,000 claim while any avoidable preference is unpaid; UNVERIFIED (not in the library, flagged not cited): whether post-petition payment of Mesa's §503(b)(9) claim erodes the (c)(4) shield.

The demanded amount was also inflated by 85,000 (gross invoiced 210,000 without crediting the 85,000 paid).

2026-03-18 email to Redwood's CFO threatening to 'hold all future shipments and report to credit bureaus': threatening credit-bureau reporting to pressure payment is expressly listed in the library as an act to collect, done with knowledge of the filing.

Conditioning new shipments on payment of prepetition debt (the 03-18 hold-shipments threat and sales rep Frank's 2026-03-19 'pay first' answer to Redwood's counsel): UNVERIFIED whether a refusal to ship pending prepayment itself violates the stay — that question is outside the library. The credit-bureau threat in the same email clearly is a violation; Frank's 'pay first' is treated as a critical-vendor negotiation misstep (Kmart normal-terms problem), not a collection act.
